correctness.rationale: The two-particle subdivision criteria apply directly; inclusion of the deleted-product model is natural under relabelings. In its ordered model orient graph edges from the m-side to the n-side. A top chain is an array indexed by i,k on the m-side and j,l on the n-side, zero for i=k or j=l. The cellular boundary equations are exactly zero sums in each of the four coordinates, so top cycles are Z_m tensor Z_n, where Z_s is the space of zero-diagonal s-by-s arrays whose row and column sums vanish. Under transpose the symmetric part of Z_s is the kernel of the unordered-pair row-sum map P_s to U_s (surjective for s>=3 since sums of two distinct basis vectors span). It is B_s, including zero at s=3. The skew part is the kernel of contraction by augmentation in exterior degree two, namely the exterior square of the standard representation, C_s. Particle interchange negates simultaneous transpose because it exchanges the two oriented square directions. Rational transfer therefore gives precisely B_m tensor C_n plus C_m tensor B_n. Graph part exchange swaps those distinct summands at equal sizes, giving trace zero and the index-two induced module; at m=n=3 the homology is zero. The character and dimension follow by counting fixed unordered pairs with the proper symmetric/skew signs. Independently, the frozen Euler proof uses the correct Ko–Park H1 rank, and its equivariant total-trajectory map is surjective by moving a particle around a generating four-cycle with a spectator outside it.

A separate indexed theorem also supplies the same module by ordered-to-unordered rational transfer.
